poster.title: Poster and TV screens
poster.noAppUrl: APP_URL is not set in the .env file, so links and the QR code cannot be made. Set it to the server address (for example http://192.168.1.10:3000) and restart.
poster.noKey: DISPLAY_KEY is not set in the .env file, so TV screens cannot open the board.
poster.tvHelp: Open one of these addresses in the browser of the TV or Android TV stick, then press OK once to turn on the sound. Anyone with the link can see the board, so keep it to staff.

audit.title: Audit log
audit.intro: Who did what and when: logins, every queue action, setup changes, exports and privacy requests. It never holds patient names or phone numbers. Times are hospital time ({tz}).

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.retentionText: Each night at 02:30, patients not seen for {days} days lose their name, phone number and ABHA number. Visit counts and times are kept, so reports stay correct. Change RETENTION_DAYS in the .env file to use a different number of days.
privacy.retentionStatus: {anonymised} of {total} patients are anonymised. Last run: {lastRun}.
privacy.notYet: not yet (it also runs 2 minutes after the app starts)
privacy.consentHelp: This is shown at the desk and on the check-in page. Each token stores the version the patient agreed to, the time, and whether it was at the desk or on their own phone.

tools.title: A patient's data request

problem.title: Waiting is the real problem
problem.intro: When registration moves from paper to a token on screen, waits fall. These are reported figures from India.

a.text: Registration wait at pilot hospitals after QR-code Scan and Share registration, with about 4.06 lakh patients in 347 hospitals by February 2023. This is an official claim of the National Health Authority, not an independent study.

b.text: Average wait before seeing a doctor in Bihar after all 592 government facilities moved to electronic OPD registration (August 2024 to May 2025).

s1.d: At the desk, or by scanning a QR code on the wall with your own phone. It takes three fields.

s2.d: Sit, step out for tea, or wait at home nearby. Your phone shows how many people are ahead of you.

s3.d: Your token appears on the TV board with the room number, and a voice calls it in Hindi and English.

tokens.d: Numbered per department each day, with priority for emergencies, elderly, pregnant and disabled patients.

tv.d: Large board for any TV or Android TV stick, with a chime and a spoken call in Hindi and English. Token numbers only, never names.

doctor.d: One big Next button, plus recall, skip and no-show. Built for a busy room.

qr.d: Patients scan a poster, enter name, phone and age, and get a token on their own phone.

lang.d: Every screen works in both languages, and more can be added by translating one file.

reports.d: Daily counts, average wait and consult time, and a CSV export that holds no patient names.

privacy.title: Privacy by design
privacy.big: Names never shown on screen. Your data stays on your server.
privacy.d: QueueCare runs on a computer in your own hospital. There is no cloud account, no tracking and no outside service. Patient names and phone numbers are removed automatically after a set number of days, and every action is written to an audit log.

install.title: Install in three commands
install.d: You need one computer with Docker (2 GB of memory is enough). Then open the address of that computer on the desk PCs, phones and the TV.
install.guidePlain: Read ADMIN_GUIDE.md in the project folder

q1.a: Yes. QueueCare is open source under the MIT licence. There are no fees, no subscription and no paid services inside it. You only need a computer to run it.

q2.a: No. It works on the hospital's own Wi-Fi or LAN, because the server is a computer in the building. The spoken call uses the text-to-speech voice already in the TV or browser. Internet is only needed to download it the first time.

q3.a: You can note a patient's ABHA number at the desk. QueueCare does not connect to ABDM services by itself; it only keeps the number you type, if the patient chooses to give it.

q4.a: One computer or small server with 2 GB of memory to run it, a desk PC or phone for each clerk and doctor, and any TV or Android TV stick with a browser for the board. A 58 mm thermal printer is optional for token slips.
